pairs.rationale: DS scope subsumes DA: SQL/querying, data cleaning, dashboards, and presenting findings to management are all DS responsibilities.
DS uses BI and data-analysis software plus visualization/reporting for decision-makers, which is BI's core reporting scope.
DS applies data mining, feature selection, and machine learning to large datasets, the modeling core MLE builds on.
DS designs surveys/sampling methods and applies applied statistics, overlapping the statistician's method-selection and design work.
DA's SQL querying, dashboard building, and stakeholder reporting map almost directly onto BI's report/dashboard responsibilities.
DA's advanced SQL and dashboard building overlap AE, but AE additionally requires dbt modeling and version-controlled analytics code.
DA's SQL and analysis are a foundation, but DS additionally needs ML, feature selection, and statistical modeling DA does not cover.
BI's querying, dashboard maintenance, and stakeholder reporting cover DA's core, though DA leans more on production SQL and A/B testing.
AE's advanced SQL, data modeling, and BI dashboard delivery cover DA's core scope with room to spare.
AE's data modeling (staging/intermediate/mart), warehouse SQL, and ETL/reverse-ETL pipelines overlap DE's pipeline and warehouse work.
AE's KPI definition/instrumentation and self-service dashboard delivery are exactly BI's reporting and dashboard core.
Same SOC (15-1243.00): both design warehouse schemas/data models, set storage and access standards, and integrate new sources.
Same SOC (15-1243.00): DArch's schema/data-modeling, standards enforcement, and ETL/cloud integration are DE's day-to-day work.
DE's data modeling, warehouse SQL, and ETL pipeline development feed directly into AE's warehouse modeling and syncs.
MLE's model design/evaluation and analysis of complex unstructured datasets overlap DS's modeling and analysis responsibilities.
Statistician's method selection, sampling/experiment design, and data cleaning/weighting are DS's analytical foundation.
Statistician's data cleaning/validation, trend identification, and clear reporting map onto DA's analysis and stakeholder communication.
Statistician's experimental design, model validation, and math methods overlap OR's model formulation and validation.
OR's mathematical/simulation modeling, statistical data-requirement judgment, and validation overlap the statistician's method work.
OR's mathematical/simulation modeling and management-facing analysis overlap DS's modeling and communication of findings.
